1.outline: Term theme: 'Spreadsheet Skills'. Learn the vocabulary of a spreadsheet: cells, rows, columns, and how a cell reference like B3 works.
1.sowResources: Microsoft Excel, Google Sheets, cell-reference handout.
objectives: Name the parts of a spreadsheet: cell, row, column.
Read and write a cell reference such as B3.
Enter data into the correct cells.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Spreadsheet vocabulary
plan.detail: Label rows, columns and cells on a projected sheet. Introduce the coordinate idea: column letter, then row number.

plan.title: Cell reference practice
plan.detail: Call out a reference (e.g. C4); pupils click the matching cell and type a word.

plan.title: Enter simple data
plan.detail: Enter a small class list into a sheet, one name per row. Save and log out.

successCriteria: I can name a cell, row and column.
I can find a cell from its reference.
I entered data into the correct cells.

2.outline: Format a data table so it is easy to read: bold headers, adjusted column widths, and borders.
objectives: Bold a header row.
Adjust column width so text isn't cut off.
Add borders to make a table clear.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Format the table
plan.detail: Bold the header row, widen columns, add borders around the data.

plan.title: Before/after
plan.detail: Compare unformatted and formatted versions — which is easier to read?

plan.title: Save
plan.detail: Save and log out.

successCriteria: My header row is bold.
No text is cut off in any column.
My table has clear borders.

3.outline: Learn the =SUM() and =AVERAGE() formulas using a set of sample scores.
3.sowResources: Microsoft Excel, Google Sheets, formula reference card.
objectives: Write a =SUM formula for a range of cells.
Write an =AVERAGE formula for a range.
Explain what each formula calculates.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: What is a formula?
plan.detail: A formula starts with =. Show a formula calculate instead of just displaying text.

plan.title: SUM and AVERAGE
plan.detail: Type =SUM(B2:B10) and =AVERAGE(B2:B10) on sample scores data. Check the results make sense.

plan.title: Explain it
plan.detail: Explain to a partner what each formula does. Save and log out.

successCriteria: I wrote a working =SUM formula.
I wrote a working =AVERAGE formula.
I can explain what each formula calculates.

4.outline: Use the fill handle to copy a formula down a column, saving time entering the same calculation for every row.
objectives: Use the fill handle to copy a formula.
Check the copied formula adjusted correctly for each row.
Explain why fill-down is faster than retyping.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Fill handle demo
plan.detail: Type one formula, then drag the fill handle down to copy it to every row.

plan.title: Check the results
plan.detail: Click on a few filled cells and check the cell references changed sensibly.

plan.title: Speed comparison
plan.detail: Discuss: how much faster was fill-down than typing 10 formulas? Save and log out.

successCriteria: I used the fill handle to copy a formula.
My copied formulas give correct results.
I can explain why fill-down saves time.

5.outline: Select a data range and insert a chart, adding a title and axis labels so it is easy to understand.
5.sowResources: Microsoft Excel, Google Sheets, chart-choice poster.
objectives: Select data and insert a chart.
Add a chart title.
Label the chart axes.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Insert a chart
plan.detail: Select the data range, insert a bar chart, and add a chart title.

plan.title: Label the axes
plan.detail: Add axis labels so a reader knows what the numbers mean.

plan.title: Peer check
plan.detail: Partner checks the chart makes sense without extra explanation. Save and log out.

successCriteria: I inserted a chart from my data.
My chart has a title.
My chart's axes are labelled.

6.subtopic: Pick the Chart That Fits the Data
6.outline: Compare bar, pie and line charts on the same data and decide which one best answers the question being asked.
6.sowResources: Microsoft Excel, Google Sheets, chart-choice poster.
objectives: Build the same data as a bar, pie and line chart.
Judge which chart best answers a given question.
Justify the chart choice in one sentence.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Three chart types
plan.detail: Build the same data set as a bar chart, a pie chart and a line chart.

plan.title: Which fits?
plan.detail: Given a question (e.g. 'what share of the total is X?'), decide which chart answers it best.

plan.title: Justify it
plan.detail: Write one sentence justifying the best chart choice. Save and log out.

activities: Build bar, pie and line charts
successCriteria: I built the same data as three chart types.
I chose the chart that best answers a given question.
I justified my choice in one sentence.

7.outline: Build a small personal tracker — pocket money savings or game scores — using formulas and a chart to show progress.
7.sowResources: Microsoft Excel, Google Sheets, tracker exemplar.
objectives: Design a simple personal tracker.
Use a formula to total or average the entries.
Add a chart showing progress.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Build the tracker
plan.detail: Set up columns for dates/entries and amounts, add a running total formula.

plan.title: Add a chart
plan.detail: Chart the tracker so progress is visible at a glance.

plan.title: Save
plan.detail: Save and log out.

successCriteria: My tracker has clear columns for entries.
My tracker uses a working total or average formula.
My tracker has a chart showing progress.

8.outline: Finish and tidy the term's portfolio piece: a working spreadsheet using SUM and AVERAGE with a suitable, correctly labelled chart.
8.sowResources: Microsoft Excel, Google Sheets, portfolio folder.
objectives: Finish a spreadsheet using SUM and AVERAGE.
Check the chart is suitable and correctly labelled.
Save the finished piece to the portfolio folder.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Finish the portfolio piece
plan.detail: Complete the tracker or a new dataset with SUM, AVERAGE and a labelled chart.

plan.title: Rubric self-check
plan.detail: Check against the assessment rubric: formulas correct, chart suitable and labelled.

plan.title: Save
plan.detail: Save to the portfolio folder. Log out.

successCriteria: My spreadsheet uses SUM and AVERAGE correctly.
My chart is suitable for the data and labelled.
My finished piece is saved to the portfolio folder.

9.outline: Extend the portfolio spreadsheet with =MAX and =MIN formulas to find the highest and lowest values, adding a short written insight.
objectives: Write =MAX and =MIN formulas.
Identify the highest and lowest values in the data.
Write one sentence explaining what the data shows.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: MAX and MIN
plan.detail: Add =MAX and =MIN formulas to the portfolio spreadsheet.

plan.title: Write an insight
plan.detail: Write one sentence explaining what the highest/lowest values tell you.

plan.title: Save
plan.detail: Save and log out.

successCriteria: My spreadsheet has working MAX and MIN formulas.
I identified the highest and lowest values.
I wrote one sentence explaining the insight.

10.outline: Rehearse the term's spreadsheet skills in pairs: enter data, format it, add formulas, build a chart.
10.sowResources: Recap slide deck, practice task cards.
objectives: Recall the term's spreadsheet skills in order.
Rehearse entering data, formulas and a chart with a partner.
Identify the trickiest step.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Skill recap
plan.detail: Recap: enter data, format, SUM/AVERAGE, chart — as a class chant.

plan.title: Paired rehearsal
plan.detail: Build a small dataset with formulas and a chart with a partner reading the task card, then swap.

plan.title: Tricky step check
plan.detail: Name the step you still find hardest. Log out.

successCriteria: I can list the term's spreadsheet steps in order.
I rehearsed the practical task with a partner.
I know which step needs more practice.

11.outline: Individual task: enter data correctly, use =SUM and =AVERAGE, and create a suitable, correctly labelled chart.
objectives: Enter data correctly into a spreadsheet.
Use SUM and AVERAGE formulas correctly.
Create a suitable chart with a title and labels.

plan.title: Settle and explain
plan.detail: Calm start — explain the task and rubric.

plan.title: Build the spreadsheet
plan.detail: Individual practical: enter given data, apply SUM/AVERAGE, insert a labelled chart.

plan.title: Save and check
plan.detail: Save with the correct file name and double-check the formulas calculate correctly.

plan.title: Celebrate
plan.detail: Celebrate the term's progress. Log out.

successCriteria: I entered the data correctly.
My SUM and AVERAGE formulas give correct results.
My chart is suitable, titled and labelled.
